messages.author: e1287a7843032e0f
messages.subject: unmarkedFrameGDS error
parts:
The issue I am having is with the error: "Some observations have been discarded because correspoding covariates were missing." I've seen similar questions come up in a few discussions, but different unmarked programs, and I haven't been able to utilize those discussions to fix my issue.

I am working on a hierarchical distance analysis of 60 points, each sampled 3-11 times (y). Points are assigned into one of two habitat categories (siteCovs), and survey-specific covariates are included (Julian Date, Minutes After Sunrise [MAS], and Wind [low or high]). Other than the uneven sampling, there is no missing data.

umf <- unmarkedFrameGDS(y=y, siteCovs=covs, yearlySiteCovs=list(Obs=surveyor.df, Wind=wind.df, MAS=mas.df, Julian=julian.df), survey="point", unitsIn="m", dist.breaks=breaks, numPrimary=T)

In running the model p1, there is no issue. But p2, ph1, and phi2 returns the error.
p1 <- gdistsamp(~1, ~1, ~1, umf, keyfun="halfnorm", output="density", unitsOut="ha", K=50)
p2 <- gdistsamp(~1, ~1, ~Wind, umf, keyfun="halfnorm", output="density", unitsOut="ha", K=50)
phi1 <- gdistsamp(~1, ~MAS, ~1, umf, keyfun="halfnorm", output="density", unitsOut="ha", K=50)
phi2 <- gdistsamp(~1, ~Julian, ~1, umf, keyfun="halfnorm", output="density", unitsOut="ha", K=50)

The outputs otherwise appear reasonably valid. But this error creates problems in using additional code to compile AIC tables (*) and using model averaging approaches. Any suggestions would be welcomed!

* "Data are not the same among models due to missing covariate values. Consider removing NAs before analysis."

Thanks,
Erik

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] unmarkedFrameGDS error
parts:
You and gdistsamp certainly have different opinions about missing data.  I think the only way to solve the problem is to share your data.  If that's not appropriate to share here, I'd be happy to take a look at it offline.

Jim

messages.author: e1287a7843032e0f
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] unmarkedFrameGDS error
parts:
All – Jim was kind enough to work off-list with me on this, and the solution turned out that my yearlySiteCovs were data frames and had to be converted to matrices. One of my data frames included a character variable, so I converted that to dummy variables first, and then to a matrix. The code now works! Thanks, Jim!

 

Cheers,

Erik
